name: Ehlers-Danlos Syndromes (EDS)
inheritance: Autosomal dominant or recessive depending on subtype
description: A group of hereditary connective tissue disorders characterized by joint hypermobility, skin hyperextensibility, and generalized tissue fragility caused by defects in collagen synthesis or structure.
diagnostic_considerations: Beighton score evaluation, clinical subtype differentiation, targeted next-generation genetic sequencing panels.

name: Fabry Disease
typical_symptoms: burning neuropathic pain in hands and feet
description: An X-linked lysosomal storage disorder caused by deficient alpha-galactosidase A (GLA) activity, leading to globotriaosylceramide (Gb3) accumulation in vascular endothelium and tissues.
diagnostic_considerations: Alpha-galactosidase A enzyme activity assay in males, GLA gene sequence analysis in males and females, urinary or plasma lyso-Gb3 biomarker.

name: Wilson Disease
description: An autosomal recessive error of copper metabolism due to mutations in the ATP7B gene, leading to excessive copper deposition primarily in the liver, brain, and corneas.
diagnostic_considerations: Slit-lamp examination for Kayser-Fleischer rings, serum ceruloplasmin, 24-hour urinary copper excretion, liver biopsy for quantitative copper, ATP7B genetic testing.

name: Marfan Syndrome
description: An autosomal dominant systemic disorder of connective tissue caused by pathogenic variants in the FBN1 gene encoding fibrillin-1, predominantly affecting cardiovascular, ocular, and skeletal systems.
diagnostic_considerations: Revised Ghent Criteria, echocardiography of aortic root and ascending aorta, slit-lamp ophthalmologic exam, FBN1 sequencing.

name: Gaucher Disease
description: A hereditary metabolic condition caused by a deficiency of the lysosomal enzyme beta-glucocerebrosidase (GBA gene), causing lipid-laden macrophages (Gaucher cells) to accumulate in the spleen, liver, and bone marrow.
diagnostic_considerations: Beta-glucosidase enzyme activity assay in peripheral blood leukocytes, GBA targeted mutation or sequencing, bone imaging (DEXA, MRI).

name: Alkaptonuria
typical_symptoms: dark urine on exposure to air
ochronosis (dark pigmentation of cartilage and sclera)
description: A rare autosomal recessive metabolic disorder caused by deficiency of homogentisate 1,2-dioxygenase (HGD gene), causing homogentisic acid accumulation in collagenous tissues and urine.
diagnostic_considerations: Urinary organic acid analysis by GC-MS detecting elevated homogentisic acid, clinical observation of urine darkening with alkalinization, HGD gene analysis.

name: Pompe Disease (Glycogen Storage Disease Type II)
description: An autosomal recessive lysosomal storage disease resulting from deficiency of acid alpha-glucosidase (GAA), leading to lysosomal glycogen accumulation in skeletal and cardiac muscle.
diagnostic_considerations: Acid alpha-glucosidase enzyme activity assay (DBS or leukocytes), GAA gene sequencing, electromyography, pulmonary function tests.
